lead.headline: Computer games claim the brightest shelf space
lead.dek: As February closes, Computer Gaming World points readers toward deeper strategy and adventure titles while home-computer stores keep selling machines through games, BASIC, and office software promises.
lead.body: During the week of February 21-27, 1983, the home-computer story is not a single launch so much as a crowded shelf. Computer Gaming World's winter issue keeps strategy, simulation, and adventure games in front of serious players, with Serpentine, Cosmic Balance, S.E.U.I.S., Armor Assault, and other computer titles showing how far the market had moved beyond simple arcade imitation. Across the same counter, Lotus 1-2-3 was still fresh for IBM PC shoppers after its January on-sale date, while Commodore, TI, and Atari machines competed for families through memory, price, games, and programming.
